result.summary: This PR adds functional test coverage for the bitcoin wrapper's argument-handling paths (version, help, no command, unknown command, unknown option) that currently return without calling exec and are therefore untested and invisible to coverage tooling. A second commit fixes a bug in the new tests' run_wrapper helper so it correctly runs under valgrind_cmd, matching other tests in the file.
result.problem: The bitcoin wrapper's own argument parsing has no test coverage; five early-return branches (version, help, no-command, unknown command, unknown option) are never exercised, leaving bugs in wrapper argument handling to reach users undetected until runtime.

resolved_concerns: mercie-ux pointed out that run_wrapper bypassed node.binaries.valgrind_cmd, meaning the new tests didn't run under valgrind despite --valgrind being passed; author pushed a fix using valgrind_cmd and confirmed timing matches expectations.

categories.rationale: Closes a real, previously undocumented gap: the description notes src/bitcoin.cpp is absent from coverage reports entirely and five branches (version, help, no-command, unknown command/option) were never exercised, per the commit message 'the paths that return without exec ... are never run.' This is a worthwhile but narrow addition to a small wrapper tool, not high-risk code, so it sits at P3 rather than higher; the valgrind_cmd fix is a minor correctness improvement to the test itself.

result.card: This PR adds functional test coverage for the bitcoin wrapper's argument-handling paths (version, help, no command, unknown command, unknown option), which the description states leaves src/bitcoin.cpp entirely absent from coverage reports because exec replaces the process before coverage flushes. A second commit fixes a bug where the new tests bypassed valgrind_cmd, caught by reviewer mercie-ux and promptly fixed by the author. The PR is small, self-contained, and ready for review with no open concerns. It conflicts at the file level with two other open PRs (#36190, #36106) touching the same wrapper area, which may require coordination or rebase but does not block review now.
